newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians get phone code -- but don't call yet.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians get phone code -- but don't call yet.

text.p: The Palestinian self-rule areas have been granted an international telephone country code of their own -- but don't dial just yet.

"I am pleased to inform you that the Telecommunication Standardization Bureau (TSB) has made a temporary reservation of country code 970 for Palestine," director Th. Irmer wrote to Palestinian Telecommunications Minister Imad al-Falouji.
All calls to Palestinians go through Israel, which has 972 for its country code.
The TSB said that it was a provisional allocation of a country code contingent on Israel and the PLO coming to terms on an independent Palestinian phone network, as agreed in a 1995 peace deal.
Falouji said Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority would soon approach Israel on establishing a network for the West Bank and Gaza Strip separate from the Israeli company Bezeq.
